newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian rebels blame Berisha for scrubbed trip.
newsitem.headline: Albanian rebels blame Berisha for scrubbed trip.

text.p: A top local leader in the rebel-held Albanian port of Vlore said on Thursday he was disappointed international mediator Franz Vranitzky had cancelled his trip to the south of the anarchic Balkan state.
Medin Xhelili, head of a regional council in Vlore, said Albanian President Sali Berisha was to blame for Vranitzky's last-minute decision to cancel the trip planned for Thursday.
He said thousands of people in Vlore were planning to greet Vranitzky, envoy for the Organisation of Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), on his first trip to the south.
Xhelili led more than 10,000 people in welcoming Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi on his visit to Vlore on Sunday.
"Berisha is plotting against the government and its spirit of reconciliation," Xhelili told Reuters.

Berisha appointed an all-party government last month after armed rebels seized control of the south. The government, which aims to organise early elections by June, is headed by Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, who is from the south.
"There are two powers in Albania, one is the Prime Minister Bashkim Fino's government and the other is Berisha's regime," Xhelili said. "Berisha wants to (under)mine activity of Fino's cabinet."

Vranitzky decided after meeting Berisha on Wednesday evening not to travel to Vlore, a hotbed of anti-Berisha feeling, or to the northern town of Skhoder as planned on Thursday, his spokeswoman Melissa Fleming said.
The former Austrian chancellor wanted to focus his two-day trip to Albania "on the situation here and on preparing for elections," she said. She said Vranitzky would visit the south on a later trip.
Berisha said rebel committees controlling much of southern Albania were hindering progress towards the vote and must be disbanded.

Rebels seized control of the south earlier this year. They blame Berisha for the pyramid schemes which cost many Albanians their savings. Nearly 300 were killed in unchecked violence after people looted arsenals deserted by police and troops.
